question.text: In the figure, three massless strings meet at a common knot. A horizontal string connects the knot to a fixed wall; the tension in this string is 30 N. A second string runs from the knot up to a fixed support, making a 45° angle with the vertical. A third string hangs straight down from the knot and supports a block of weight W. Find W.
conditions: tension in the horizontal string is 30 N
the inclined string makes a 45° angle with the vertical
the vertical string holds the block directly below the knot

figure.description: Three massless strings are tied together at one knot. A horizontal string runs from the knot to a fixed vertical wall. An inclined string runs from the same knot up to a fixed support, making a 45° angle with the vertical direction. A third string hangs straight down from the knot, with a block of weight W tied to its lower end.

solution.approach: At the knot, resolve the diagonal string's tension along the horizontal and vertical directions and balance each against the known tension and the hanging weight.

steps.text: At the knot, three strings pull: the diagonal string at 45° from the vertical, the horizontal string with tension 30 N, and the vertical string carrying weight W.
Balance the horizontal direction: the diagonal string's horizontal component equals the horizontal string's tension.
Solve for the diagonal string's tension T.
Balance the vertical direction: the diagonal string's vertical component supports the weight W.

common_mistakes.text: Resolving the 45° string's components the wrong way round (using cos45° for the horizontal part) still gives 30 N here only because sin45° = cos45°; at any other angle this swap gives a wrong W.
Setting W equal to the full diagonal tension T = 30√2 N ≈ 42.4 N, instead of only its vertical component.
